items.text: 25 May 1973 — Continuous maps from functors
A map $f\colon X\to Y$ gives $f^*\colon\operatorname{Top}(Y)\to\operatorname{Top}(X)$: left exact, commutes with direct limits (so has the adjoint $f_*$).
$f^*$ is defined up to isomorphism only. Assume $X,Y$ sober.
X=\{\text{fibre functors on }\operatorname{Top}(X)\}/\simeq,\qquad Y=\{\text{fibre functors on }\operatorname{Top}(Y)\}/\simeq
f\colon\varepsilon\longmapsto\varepsilon\circ f^*
Because $(f^*F)_x=F_{f(x)}$.
Converse: every such $f^*$ (left exact, commuting with direct limits) comes from a unique continuous $f$.
Compose fibre functors with $f^*$: a map $f_0\colon X\to Y$; continuous (topologies come from subobjects of $e$, which a left exact functor preserves).
Show $f^*\simeq f_0^*$: both commute with direct limits, and opens of $Y$ generate: enough on $\mathcal O(Y)$.
f^*|_{\mathcal O(Y)},\ f_0^*|_{\mathcal O(Y)}\colon \mathcal O(Y)\to\mathcal O(X)\ \text{both } V\mapsto f_0^{-1}(V)
\{\text{continuous maps } X\to Y\}\ \simeq\ \{\text{functors } \operatorname{Top}(Y)\to\operatorname{Top}(X)\ \text{left exact, preserving direct limits}\}/\!\simeq
Isomorphism classes only? Such functors have no non-trivial automorphisms; but there are homomorphisms $f\to g$ between functors.
For Hausdorff spaces: none unless $f=g$. For schemes (points rarely closed): there are, described later.
Composition of maps = composition of the functors.
$X=\mathrm{pt}$: a point of $Y$ = a fibre functor on $\operatorname{Top}(Y)$.
Definition of a topos
A generalisation: keep the properties of categories of sheaves.
$E$ is a topos if it has the exactness properties of $\mathbf{Sets}$ for direct limits and finite inverse limits, plus a small generating set.
$C\subset\operatorname{Ob}E$ small, generating:
E\longrightarrow \hat C,\qquad X\mapsto\bigl(Z\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)\bigr)_{Z\in C}\quad\text{conservative}
Equivalent (given kernels, fibre products, strict epimorphic families): conservative on monos, faithful, fully faithful.
Giraud's characterisation
First definition used sheaves on a site. Giraud: exactness axioms suffice.
(a) $E$ has (finite, indeed all small) inverse limits.
(b) Arbitrary small sums exist, disjoint and universal.
Universal: stable under base change. $X=\coprod X_i$, $X'\to X$:
X'_i=X_i\times_X X',\qquad \coprod_i X'_i\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }X'
Disjoint:
X_i\times_X X_j=\varnothing_E\ \ (i\neq j),\qquad X_i\times_X X_i=X_i\ \ (X_i\to X\ \text{mono})
$\varnothing_E$: the initial object, as the empty set in $\mathbf{Sets}$.
(c) Equivalence relations are effective and universal.
R\subset X\times X,\quad R(Z)\ \text{an equivalence relation on } X(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)
R\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}X\times_Y X,\qquad Y=\operatorname{coker}(R\rightrightarrows X)
Universal: $X\to Y$ stays an epimorphism after any base change $Y'\to Y$; $Y'$ is the quotient of $X'$ by $R'$.
(d) There is a small generating subcategory $C$.
Consequences: the subobjects of $X$ form a set, so do the quotients.
$E_{ab}$ is abelian with exact filtering direct limits and a small generating set (a single generator: their sum): enough injectives.
Also in $E$ itself: an injective abelian object is injective as an object.
Topoi are taken up to equivalence ($E\xrightarrow{\simeq}E'$ with a double tilde), not isomorphism.
Replaces « up to homeomorphism ».
Invariants of a topos
Two distinguished objects: initial $\varnothing_E$ and final $e_E$; one arrow between them.
\Gamma(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_E(e,X)\qquad\text{sections}
H^i(E,-)=R^i\Gamma\colon E_{ab}\to\mathbf{Ab}
A set $I$: the constant object $I_E=\coprod_I e$, left exact and preserving direct limits.
H^i(E,M_0)=H^i(E,M_{0,E})\qquad M_0\ \text{an abelian group}
Homotopy invariants via Čech processes (Artin–Mazur): pro-groups.
Algebraic topology can be done with topoi. Now: many examples (SGA 4 has many exercises).
Examples
0. $\operatorname{Top}(X)$ for a space $X$: the model.
The empty topos
\operatorname{Top}(\varnothing)=\{\text{one-element sets}\}\ \simeq\ \text{one-point category}
The empty topos $\operatorname{Top}(0)$: the category is not empty (it has $\varnothing_E$, $e_E$), but
E\ \text{empty topos}\iff \varnothing_E\to e_E\ \text{isomorphism}
Two pictures: the category $E$, and the generalised space « underneath ».
Will be the initial topos.
The point topos
\operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt})\ \simeq\ \mathbf{Sets},\qquad F\mapsto F(\mathrm{pt})=F_x
The one-point topos $\operatorname{Top}(1)$ — the final topos. Equivalently:
\mathbf{Sets}\xrightarrow{\ I\mapsto I_E\ }E\ \ \text{is an equivalence}
Its category is as big as $\mathbf{Sets}$; the topos is small — a point.
Sheaves with a group action
$X$ a space, $G$ a discrete group acting on $X$.
\operatorname{Top}(X,G)=\{\text{étale } X'\to X\ \text{with a } G\text{-action over the action on } X\}
A topos: (a)-(d) are inherited from étale spaces.
$G=1$: $\operatorname{Top}(X)$. $X=\mathrm{pt}$:
B_G=\operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt},G)=\{G\text{-sets}\}\qquad\text{classifying topos}
Abelian objects = $G$-modules; $e$ = the point with its $G$-action.
\Gamma(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}_G(e,Z)=Z^{G}\ (\text{invariants})
H^i(B_G,M)=H^i(G,M)\qquad\text{group cohomology}
The same as the cohomology of the classifying space of $G$, but the topos is canonically defined.
H^i(X;G,M)\qquad\text{(old Tôhoku paper)}
Spectral sequences: morphisms between topoi — defined later.
